record.original_question: Does there exist a measurable set Omega subset R with 0 < mes(Omega) < +infinity such that its indicator function 1_Omega tiles R by translations over a set Lambda subset R that does not have periodic structure, either at level one or, more weakly, at some other integer level w? Here, not having periodic structure means that Lambda cannot be written as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions a_j Z + b_j with a_j > 0.

evidence.quote: Does there exist a measurable set Omega subset R, 0 < mes(Omega) < +infinity, whose indicator function 1_Omega can tile at level one, or, a weaker requirement, at some other integer level w, with a translation set Lambda subset R that does not have a periodic structure?

We say that a set Lambda subset R has a periodic structure if it can be represented as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions, namely Lambda = union from j=1 to N of (a_j Z + b_j), where a_j, b_j are real numbers and a_j > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{R}$ be the real line equipped with Lebesgue measure $\operatorname{mes}$. For a measurable set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}$ with $0<\operatorname{mes}(\Omega)<+\infty$, let $\mathbf{1}_\Omega$ denote its indicator function. Given a discrete set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ and a positive integer $w$, we say that $\mathbf{1}_\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ by translations along $\Lambda$ at level $w$ if
$$\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathbf{1}_\Omega(x-\lambda)=w\qquad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb{R}.$$
The case $w=1$ corresponds to a partition (modulo measure zero) of $\mathbb{R}$ into translates of $\Omega$.

Say that a set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ has periodic structure if it can be written as a disjoint union
$$\Lambda=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^{N}\bigl(a_j\mathbb{Z}+b_j\bigr)$$
of finitely many arithmetic progressions, where $a_j>0$ and $b_j\in\mathbb{R}$. Otherwise, $\Lambda$ is said to lack periodic structure.

Question: Does there exist a measurable set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}$ with $0<\operatorname{mes}(\Omega)<+\infty$, a positive integer $w$, and a translation set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ lacking periodic structure such that $\mathbf{1}_\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ along $\Lambda$ at level $w$? In particular, can this be achieved at level $w=1$?
artifact.category_tag: translational tilings of the real line
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey on tilings by translates of a function. Subsequent work (e.g., on periodicity of low-complexity tilings, and counterexamples to the periodic tiling conjecture in higher dimensions by Greenfeld–Tao) has not, to current knowledge, resolved this one-dimensional question for indicator functions of finite-measure sets, which would necessarily be unbounded. No paper found claims a construction or a proof of impossibility on $\mathbb{R}$ at any integer level $w$.

status_evidence.title: Tiling by translates of a function: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing the question of aperiodic indicator-function tilings of R as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly stated as open.

status_evidence.title: Some variants of the periodic tiling conjecture - Terence Tao
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses variants of periodic tiling conjecture; one-dimensional indicator-function aperiodicity question is not reported as resolved.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the 1D indicator aperiodic tiling question is announced in recent variant studies.

status_evidence.title: A counterexample to the periodic tiling conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Greenfeld–Tao construct aperiodic tilings in high dimensions; the 1D case for indicator functions remains the classical setting.
status_evidence.claim: Aperiodic counterexamples are constructed in high dimensions, not on R.
